security_spec.violation_condition: Linux kernel context-switch path saves/restores only the sivt BASE field without preserving the EHV bit, or kernel code writes sivt with a hardcoded value that clears EHV (e.g., masking bits [5:0]), causing one task's synchronous exception vectoring configuration to leak into another task or be silently disabled.
security_spec.summary: sivt CSR gains EHV control bit at bit 0: kernel must save/restore full sivt (not just BASE) on context switch, or synchronous exceptions (page faults, ecalls) from one task may be vectored through another task's handler table, leaking control flow.

findings.finding: CSR_SIVT (0x107) is not defined. Only CSR_STVEC (0x105) is defined at line 321. The Ssivt/Smehv extension CSR (sivt at 0x107, containing the interrupt vector table BASE and the EHV bit) has no constant definition in the kernel, meaning no kernel code can reference or manage this CSR. If Smehv is enabled on hardware, the kernel cannot save/restore this state.

findings.finding: The __switch_to context-switch path saves/restores GPRs (ra, sp, s0-s11), the SUM bit in sstatus, and the shadow call stack pointer, but does NOT save/restore the sivt CSR. On hardware implementing Ssivt/Smehv, if a task configures sivt.EHV for synchronous exception hardware vectoring, that configuration will leak to the next scheduled task on the same hart. Similarly, task-specific sivt BASE addresses would not be preserved across context switches.
findings.snippet:
SYM_FUNC_START(__switch_to)
	/* Save context into prev->thread */
	li    a4,  TASK_THREAD_RA
	add   a3, a0, a4
	add   a4, a1, a4
	REG_S ra,  TASK_THREAD_RA_RA(a3)
	/* ... GPR save/restore only ... no sivt handling */

findings.finding: The switch_to macro chains __switch_to_fpu, __switch_to_vector, __switch_to_envcfg, and __switch_to but has no hook for saving/restoring sivt (or seivt). The thread_struct has no field for sivt state. If Ssivt/Smehv support is added, this macro and thread_struct must be extended to context-switch the sivt CSR (including the EHV bit in bits [1:0] per the spec).

findings.finding: thread_struct has no field to persist sivt CSR state across context switches. The struct only tracks envcfg for the Xlinuxenvcfg extension. Without a thread_struct.sivt field, there is no place to save/restore per-task sivt configuration (BASE + EHV bit). Any Smehv enablement patch must add such a field.

suspend_save_csrs saves CSR_TVEC (which maps to CSR_STVEC=0x105) but does NOT save CSR_SIVT (0x107). On Ssivt/Smehv hardware, CPU suspend/resume (including hibernation) would lose the sivt configuration, silently clearing any EHV setting and reverting the interrupt vector table base address.

The suspend_context struct has no field for sivt state. Only tvec (CSR_STVEC), ie, envcfg, satp, and stimecmp are tracked. If Smehv is enabled, suspend/resume and hibernation paths would silently lose the sivt configuration including the EHV bit.

findings.finding: KVM VCPU world-switch saves/restores host STVEC (CSR_STVEC=0x105) but does not save/restore host SIVT (0x107). The host's sivt CSR (including EHV) is not preserved across VCPU guest entry/exit. If the host kernel uses Smehv, entering a guest would expose the host's sivt state to the guest or lose it on return.

kvm_arch_vcpu_load writes VS-level CSRs (VSTVEC, VSSTATUS, etc.) but does not handle the host SIVT or guest VSIVT. KVM does not virtualize the Ssivt/Smehv extension — there is no CSR_VSIVT definition, no guest_sivt field in kvm_vcpu_csr, and no save/restore logic. A guest that uses Smehv would have its sivt state silently unvirtualized.
